biodiversity_overview.text: 5,805 GBIF occurrence records for 49 tracked species are attributed to Himachal Pradesh, spanning 1856-2026.
5,704 of these records (98.3%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 22, Magnoliopsida 9, Mammalia 8, Squamata 4, Testudines 3, Amphibia 2, Pinopsida 1.

threatened_species.text: 6 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.
1 further species are threatened according to the project's unverified reference list: Tiger (EN).

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian White-eye (1,716), Indian Grey-Hornbill (754), Indian Blue Robin (605), Indian Paradise-flycatcher (601), Common Peafowl (259).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 302 in 2016 to 96 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 14.36% of Himachal Pradesh's area (40 areas intersect the state).
12.6% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (716 of 5,704); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Indian Softshell Turtle (0.49), Indian Gooseberry (0.35), Common Cat Snake (0.35), Acacia-tree (0.26), Common Leopard (0.25).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Himachal Pradesh (equal-weight reference): cell near 31.125N 76.875E (overall rank 154, median rank across weightings 169); cell near 31.875N 76.125E (overall rank 179, median rank across weightings 192); cell near 31.875N 76.875E (overall rank 359, median rank across weightings 334).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 13,694 km2 (24.48% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

57.5 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (0.42% of the 2000 extent; 0.11% in 2015-2024, rank 27 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2012 (7.17 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 0.62% of land and population density is 134.1 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
34% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.
